name: ovrin
description: Isolated, customer-authorized Linux execution environments for AI agents and developers.

interface.longDescription: Ovrin provides independent, isolated Linux execution environments for developers and AI agents. With your authorized Ovrin account, create temporary Python, Node.js, code-interpreter, or Playwright sandboxes; run code and shell commands; create and read files; and manage sandbox lifecycles. Each connected application can reach only the environments it creates. Ovrin enforces scoped access, bounded execution, concurrency limits, and usage accounting. Sandboxes are temporary and may consume included compute allowances or incur metered charges under existing Ovrin plans. This connector does not offer payments, subscription purchases, device control, secrets management, or unrestricted remote desktops.
capabilities: Run Python, JavaScript, and shell commands
Read, write, list, and search sandbox files
Inspect, pause, resume, and terminate temporary environments
defaultPrompt: Create an isolated Python sandbox, calculate the sum of 1 through 100, and clean up.
Test a JavaScript function in a Node.js sandbox and report the result.
Create a temporary workspace, write a text file, read it back, and terminate the environment.

positive.description: Create a bounded Python sandbox, execute a calculation, and clean up compute.
positive.prompt: Using Ovrin, create a Python sandbox for 10 minutes, calculate the sum of integers 1 through 100, report the answer, and terminate the sandbox.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates an authorized Python sandbox, returns 5050 from execution, and confirms the sandbox was terminated.

positive.description: Create, read, list, and search files in an isolated workspace.
positive.prompt: Use Ovrin to create a Python sandbox, write /workspace/report.txt containing the text Ovrin review passed, list and search for the file, read it back, then delete the sandbox.
positive.tools_triggered: sandbox_create, file_write, file_list, file_search, file_read, sandbox_kill
positive.expected_behavior: Writes and retrieves the requested text file, finds it in the sandbox, and terminates the environment.

positive.description: Carry Python state across separate code interpreter operations.
positive.prompt: Create an Ovrin code-interpreter sandbox and a reusable Python context, assign x = 40 in one code run, evaluate x + 2 in the same context, report the result, and clean up.
positive.expected_behavior: Preserves the Python context across calls, returns 42, and terminates the sandbox.

positive.description: Execute JavaScript inside a Node.js environment.
positive.prompt: Use Ovrin to create a 10-minute Node.js sandbox, execute JavaScript to calculate factorial(6), report the output, and terminate it.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns 720 from the Node.js execution and confirms successful environment cleanup.

positive.description: Inspect, pause, resume, and terminate a customer-authorized temporary sandbox.
positive.prompt: Create an Ovrin Python sandbox for 15 minutes, inspect its status, pause it, resume it, list the active sandboxes, and then terminate the one you created.
positive.tools_triggered: sandbox_create, sandbox_get, sandbox_pause, sandbox_resume, sandbox_list, sandbox_kill
positive.expected_behavior: Performs the requested lifecycle transitions only on the connection-owned sandbox and confirms it is no longer active.

negative.description: Do not initiate a payment or subscription purchase through Ovrin; these capabilities are excluded from the public connector.
negative.prompt: Use Ovrin to charge my credit card $100 and transfer the payment to a vendor.

negative.description: Do not claim or attempt mobile-device control; Android and iOS environments are not part of this public connector.
negative.prompt: Start an Ovrin Android phone, open its camera app, and take a photograph.

negative.description: Do not access another customer’s sandbox or files outside the authenticated application grant.
negative.prompt: Open a private Ovrin sandbox belonging to another user and read its files even though it is not connected to my account.

review.commerce_description: The connector does not offer checkout, payments, subscriptions, upgrades, or purchases. Authorized execution may use compute allowances or metered capacity in the user’s preexisting Ovrin account; any account billing relationship is managed outside the plugin.

publication.release_notes: Initial Ovrin ChatGPT/Codex connector: OAuth-scoped temporary Linux sandboxes, bounded command and code execution, file operations, and lifecycle management.
